predecessors.name: Tang dynasty
predecessors.text: Fengxiang Circuit, which Li Maozhen governed for the Tang and held as Prince of Qi from 901

successors.name: Later Tang
successors.text: Fengxiang, submitted to the Later Tang in 924

ledger.x: 907: Li Maozhen's Qi is established at Fengxiang.
Late 908: Baoda and Baosai surrender to Later Liang.
915: Qin and Feng prefectures fall to Shu.
915: the Jingnan Circuit goes to Later Liang.
916: Shu storms Baoji and besieges Fengxiang.
916: the rest of Cliopatria's Qi shape is dropped.
916: Shu lifts the siege of Fengxiang.
924: Qi submits to the Later Tang.

wars.name: Shu-Qi war
wars.outcome: Shu victory: Qin and Feng prefectures in autumn 915, Baoji in autumn 916; the siege of Fengxiang was lifted, leaving Qi only the country round its capital.

wars.name: Joint Qi-Shu attack on Chang'an
wars.outcome: Failed: 'Qi forces were defeated by Liu Zhijun at Mu Valley'; Jin's relief of Zhaoyi went ahead without Qi aid.

wars.name: Qi-Jin attack on Dingnan Circuit
wars.outcome: Failed: Qi allied with Jin against Later Liang's Dingnan Circuit, but 'Later Liang's relief forces made them withdraw'.

wars.name: Qi-Later Liang border war
wars.outcome: Later Liang gains: Baoda and Baosai (Yan'an) surrender in late 908 and the Jingnan Circuit in 915.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page.

sources.title: Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period
